'''George Leitmann''' (May 24, 1925 – May 19, 2025) was an Austrian-born American engineering scientist and educator.

==Background==
Leitmann was born on May 24, 1925, to a fully assimilated Jewish family in [[Vienna, Austria]]. His paternal grandfather was a career officer with the rank of lieutenant colonel in the [[Imperial Austrian Army (1806–1867)|Imperial Army]]. His father had been a volunteer in the [[Austro-Hungarian Army|Austrian Army]] in [[World War I]] and was wounded twice on the [[Serbian campaign|Serbian front]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=George Leitmann 'Engineering Science, Risk and Relationships at UC Berkeley and Beyond' transcript of interviews conducted by Paul Burnett in 2018 and 2019, Oral History Center of the Bancroft Library, University of California, Berkeley|url=https://digitalassets.lib.berkeley.edu/roho/ucb/text/leitmann_george_2019.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Eleven of George Leitmann's oral history interview videos| website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZ3zavgm7wigVC3cpfZGamIm24yOH15ON}}</ref>

Nonetheless, by the spring of 1940 the situation in [[Austria within Nazi Germany|Austria]] had become so dangerous that Leitmann's father fled to neighboring [[Kingdom of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], still an independent kingdom, and the rest of the family, Leitmann, his mother and two grandmothers, were able to emigrate to the US in April 1940. Tragically, [[World War II in Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia was occupied by Germany a year later]] and Leitmann's father was murdered in a [[Crveni Krst concentration camp|concentration camp in Niš, Serbia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=National Museum ~ Niš: Jewish Prisoners of the Concentration Camp "Red Cross", Author: Zoran Milentijević, 1978; translated by Dušan M. Stipanović}}</ref>

Leitmann attended a Technical High School in New York from which he graduated in December 1943, whereupon he immediately volunteered for [[United States Army|the Army]] and was inducted in February 1944 into a [[Engineer Combat Battalion|Combat Engineer Battalion]], which began its combat duties in France and Germany in late 1944. During [[Colmar Pocket|the battle of the Colmar Pocket]], Leitmann's unit was attached to the [[French First Army]] which liberated [[Colmar]]. For Leitmann's performance in this action as a member of the reconnaissance unit, he was awarded [[Croix de Guerre|the Croix de Guerre avec Palme]].

After the end of the war in Europe, Leitmann was transferred to the Army Counter-Intelligence Corps as its youngest Special Agent and, among other assignments, served as an [[Interrogation|interrogator]] at the [[Nuremberg war crimes trial|Nuremberg War Crimes Trial]]. In 1955, he married Nancy Lloyd. They had two children, son Josef, and daughter Elaine, as well as three grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.

Leitmann died on May 19, 2025, five days before turning 100.<ref>{{cite web |title=George Leitmann |url=https://www.civiccenterchapel.com/obituaries/George-Leitmann?obId=42686794 |access-date=22 May 2025 |website=Wilson & Kratzer Mortuaries, Civic Center Chapel}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 30, 2025 |title=George Leitmann, renowned academic leader, decorated WWII veteran, dies at 99 |url=https://engineering.berkeley.edu/news/2025/05/george-leitmann-renowned-academic-leader-decorated-wwii-veteran-dies-at-99/ }}</ref>

==Academic career==
After the discharge from the army in May 1946, Leitmann studied [[physics]] at [[Columbia University]] and received the [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] and [[Master of Science|MS]] degrees in 1949 and 1950, respectively. From 1950 to 1957, he was employed at the [[Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake|US Naval Ordnance Station]] (USNOTS), [[China Lake, Kern County, California|China Lake, California]], first as a physicist and then head of the aeroballistics analysis section. This assignment involved both theoretical as well as experimental research in the [[External ballistics|exterior ballistics]] of rockets. While working at USNOTS, he also enrolled in the [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] program of the [[University of California, Berkeley]], from which he received the PhD in [[Engineering physics|engineering science]] in 1956. He joined the engineering faculty at UC Berkeley in 1957 as an assistant professor, and was advanced to associate professor in 1959 and professor in 1963. He was emerited in 1991 and continued both research and university service until 2018.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Curriculum Vitae (CV)|url=https://me.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Leitmann_CV_2016.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

==Research contributions and academic services==
Leitmann contributed greatly to the theory of [[optimal control]], dynamic games, and [[operations research]], as well as applications to exterior ballistics of rockets, aerospace systems, economics, [[ecology]], [[epidemiology]], [[Counter-terrorism|counterterrorism]], and others, reported in 15 books (including ''An Introduction to Optimal Control'', ''The Calculus of Variations and Optimal Control'', ''Qualitative and Quantitative Differential Games'', and ''Cooperative and Non-cooperative Many Player Games'') and over 300 technical journal articles.<ref name=":1" /> His service to the academic community, especially the University of California, Berkeley, ranged from four Associate Deanships, Academic Senate Committee Service such as the Budget Committee, chair of the Committee on Privilege and Tenure, the first University Ombudsman during the riot-ridden late sixties, and many advisory committees such as the chair of the system-wide Advisory Committee on Research Expeditions Programs. He also served the wider academic community by service on advisory boards at other universities.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title='PERSONAGE IN SCIENCE, Professor G. Leitmann', A.A. Martynyuk, S. Pickl and H. I. Freedman, Nonlinear Dynamics and Systems Theory, 10 (3), pp. 203-210, 2010|url=https://www.e-ndst.kiev.ua/v10n3/0(32).pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Publications |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ctPjFCYDyGyBA0EHLaWxT2XDtxZb-aeD/view?usp=sharing |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date= |website=}}</ref>

==Professional services==
Leitmann held membership in many professional and government committees. He was the Founding President of the American Alexander von Humboldt Association (1994–1997). He was Co-Editor of [[Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|the Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications]] for 16 years and served as associate editor of four journals and editorial board member of eight journals.<ref name=":0" />

==Honors and awards==
The following constitutes a partial list. He was a member of the US [[National Academy of Engineering]]<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1982|url=https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/29010.aspx|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> and a Foreign or Corresponding Member of six other national Academies of Science or Engineering. He held honorary doctorates from three universities ([[University of Paris]], [[Technical University of Vienna]], and [[Technical University of Darmstadt]]). His numerous prizes and medals include: the Senior Scientist Prize, Heisenberg and Humboldt Medals of the [[Humboldt Foundation]], the [[Austrian Cross of Honor for Science and Art]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Received the Austrian Cross of Honor for Science and Art in 2013|url=https://www.facebook.com/austrianembassy/posts/professor-george-leitmann-receives-the-austrian-cross-of-honor-for-science-and-a/10151641486682833/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=[[Facebook]]}}</ref> the Levy Medal of the [[Franklin Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=13 January 2014|title=The 1981 Louis E. Levy Medal from the Franklin Institute|url=https://www.fi.edu/laureates/george-leitmann|access-date=|website=}}</ref> the Oldenburger Medal of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The 1995 Rufus Oldenburger Medal from the American Society of Mechanical Engineers|url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/rufus-oldenburger-medal|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> the first Isaacs Award (shared with Professor Y. C. Ho) of the [[International Society of Dynamic Games]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The 2004 Isaacs' Award of the International Society of Dynamic Games|url=http://www.isdg-site.org/Award|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> and the Bellman Control Heritage Award of the [[American Automatic Control Council]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The 2009 Richard E. Bellman Control Heritage Award from the American Automatic Control Council, for 'Pioneering contributions to geometric optimal control, quantitative and qualitative differential games, and stabilization and control of deterministic uncertain systems, and for exemplary service to the control field'|url=http://a2c2.org/awards/richard-e-bellman-control-heritage-award|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001032837/http://a2c2.org/awards/richard-e-bellman-control-heritage-award|archive-date=2018-10-01|access-date=|website=|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a Commander of the German and Italian Orders of Merit. In 2013 he became Chevalier de [[Legion of Honour|la Légion d'honneur]] (Knight of the Legion of Honor).<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=In 2013 the French government named Leitmann a Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur.|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVD7pBqiCMU|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>
